rationale: The expression correctly implements a double haircut (depreciation reserve plus the one-sided working-capital-release penalty via MAX(...,0)) and matches the stated hypothesis and positive sign, though it is essentially the intersection of two already-tested archive constructions and will inherit their thin ~0.07 coverage, so the incremental information is modest.

This is a near-mechanical variant of the archived Earned-Cash Discount with the retained-earnings stock swapped for its own already-tested flow (Retained Profit Accumulation Yield), and since Δre/at is essentially dividend-net ROA the signal reduces to the familiar cash-to-price × profitability composite rather than a new mechanism.

The revision is diagnostically motivated (rescaling cheapness to all claims to defuse the leverage artifact behind the weak FMB slope) and sign-consistent, but placing lt in both the valuation denominator and the productivity trend creates a mechanical shared-denominator interaction that could confound interpretation of any improvement.

The added VOL(oancf/at,3) term is one to two orders of magnitude smaller than typical price-to-sales values, so the denominator is dominated by P/S and the signal collapses to margin × sales-yield — a rediscovery of the archived Durable Margin Sales Value and Through-Cycle Margin Floor Value that already produced zero portfolio alpha.

The one-sided burn penalty is internally consistent, dimensionally sound (dollars added to dollars), and preserves the intended positive sign, but because maintenance-adjusted burn is small relative to market cap for most firms the adjustment will only re-rank a distressed minority, limiting expected incremental power over plain cash-to-price.

The construction is internally coherent — a nonnegative assets-to-market leg amplifies a signed change in liability share, so the short leg is levering-up asset-cheap firms and the long leg deleveraging ones, consistent with the negative expected sign — and it explores a genuinely different (trap-side) direction than the archive, with the main caveat that Δ(lt/at) overlaps the known debt-issuance/leverage-change anomaly and the value-leg component pulls in the opposite direction.
